summary: Elevated p99 latency and intermittent timeouts for EU traffic caused by transit AS-path change leading to cross-region hairpinning
description:
Issue summary:
Customers in EU observed a sudden increase in p99 request latency (from ~220ms to 2.5–8s) and occasional streaming disconnects / request timeouts starting 2026-03-10 08:12 UTC. Impacted endpoints: /v1/generate (streaming and non-streaming).

Impact:
- BrightDocs (enterprise) reported elevated latency and ~0.8% request timeouts over a 45-minute window.
- Internal telemetry shows p50 ~250ms, p95 ~600ms, p99 spikes to 6–8s for eu-west region; corresponding backend serving runtime CPU and GPU utilization normal.

Environment:
- prod - eu-west (primary), fallback routing via global transit to us-east observed.
- Model variants: gpt-4-realtime and redwood-small-v1; both show elevated tail latencies.

Steps to reproduce:
1. From an EU-based client (eu-west region), issue 100 streaming generation requests to /v1/generate with similar prompt load profile used by BrightDocs.
2. Observe p99 distribution in Redwood Console; compare with eu-west baseline.
3. Run traceroute and TCP captures to api-gateway from client and from internal probe in eu-west.

Observed logs / metrics (excerpt):
- Console traces: a 30–50ms TTL jump in network hop followed by 150–600ms extra RTTs for affected flows.
- Gateway logs: increased connection establishment time; more connections finishing in us-east datacenter pools.
- Netflow snapshots: AS path for several eu-west prefixes changed to transit AS 65045 -> 3356 -> 15169 (unexpected detour through us-east).

Initial hypothesis:
A transit provider (third-party peer) experienced a routing change / BGP path flap causing eu-west traffic to be re-routed through a US transit path, resulting in cross-region hairpinning and increased RTTs. Serving runtime and GPUs appear healthy, suggesting the issue is network routing rather than model performance.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:20 UTC - Support (Asha): Acknowledged issue with BrightDocs; opened ticket and escalated to SRE. First-response sent to customer with temporary mitigation steps (region pinning suggestion).

2026-03-10 08:45 UTC - SRE (Marco): Collected traceroutes and netflow from eu-west probes; observed AS path change that matches customer reports. Raising to network team and contacting transit provider. (See logs: /var/logs/network/aspath-20260310.log)

2026-03-10 09:15 UTC - Network Eng (Lena): Confirmed AS path change in provider BGP feeds; provider acknowledges a partial transit misconfiguration and is investigating. Opened provider ticket GCP-NET-8891. Redirected impacted prefixes back to preferred peering where possible.

2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Support (Asha): Sent update to BrightDocs with ETA and temporary workaround: set request header X-Region-Pref: eu-west which forces our gateway to attempt local routing; customer confirmed reduced p99 in tests but not fully resolved for all flows.
2026-03-10 11:40 UTC - SRE (Marco): Provider applied fix; internal probes show AS path restoration and p99 returning to expected range (~250–400ms). Monitoring for regression.
investigation_notes: Traceroute (eu-west probe) pre-incident: eu-peer -> eu-edge -> redwood-eu-gw -> redwood-eu-backend. Post-incident: eu-peer -> transit-us -> us-edge -> redwood-us-gw -> redwood-eu-backend (hairpin).
Netflow & BGP logs: multiple prefixes announced with new AS path that includes transit AS 3356 between 65045 and 15169. This explained additional RTT and hop count.
Serving runtime metrics: per-request token generation time unchanged; no increase in decoding time. CPU/GPU utilization normal. Points to network transpose.
Gateway routing logs: observed increase in 'remote-edge' pool usage for requests originating from eu-west; sticky routing for some customers prevented immediate failback.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-10 11:05 UTC - Transit provider confirmed and corrected BGP announcement causing AS path detour. Provider ticket GCP-NET-8891 closed by provider.

We deployed a short-term control-plane routing policy for affected enterprise tenants (BrightDocs) that prefers local-region fronting and disables automatic global fallback for critical routes. Change rolled at 2026-03-10 11:25 UTC.
Observed p99 latency reduced to baseline within ~15 minutes of provider fix and our policy change. Customers confirmed improvement.
Added postmortem action items and updated runbook: create AS-path-change alert, add automatic probe comparing expected vs observed AS path, and document manual steps to pin region per-tenant.
workaround: Customers can add X-Region-Pref: eu-west header to requests to prefer eu-fronting, or configure tenant-level region pinning in the Console under Network -> Region Preferences. These reduce exposure to transient transit detours until provider routes converge.
follow_up_actions: Create BGP/AS-path-change alert in Prometheus/Alertmanager and integrate to #incidents and PagerDuty (owner: Network Eng).
Implement automated periodic AS-path snapshotting from edge probes and compare to expected AS path map (owner: SRE).
Add tenant-level 'lock-to-region' feature to product backlog (ticket INT-525).
Review SLA wording for cross-provider network incidents and update customer communications templates.
